chapter: Learning piano, dancing and Alphonso Trent
title: Meeting Ella B. Moore and the Park Theater in Waco
summary: He meets Ella B. Moore, who calls him Willie, at the Cotton Palace shows, and sees vaudeville at the Park Theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: exposed to them. But shortly thereafter I asked my mother if I could go up and meet Ella B. Moore. Now, Ella B. Moore and Chinch Moore had a show they used to bring to the Cotton Palace in Waco--that was like a big festival they'd have, maybe for nineteen days...they'd have a big fair and they'd have a rodeo...but they always would have a colored show. And they had these people who worked on minstrels and worked on carnivals and worked on road shows. They always had some of them at these shows.

So I went up and I asked Ella B. Moore where she was from and she said, Dallas. Well, Dallas was 99 miles north of Waco. And she asked me my name, and she said, "You know, I'm going to call you Willie." I told her my name was Sammy. She said, "I'm going to call you Willie because I like you." And I promised her that someday I would make that big trip from Waco, you know, 99 miles north to see her. And she says, "Well, okay." They had a theater, a little theater in Waco called the Park Theater. Used to have vaudeville shows when they could get, You know, acts. So, that was my first introduction to a person on the stage. (Telephone interruption.) Then I met Daybreak Nelson./ Where were we?
You were talking about little theater where they...
Oh, the Gaiety Theater. So, finally my mother decided... Well, the Park Theater. The Gaiety Theater was in Waco and from time to time they had had road shows coming in.
